summary: Early-1980s CL-100-based fire lookout on Red Butte, Kaibab National Forest, Arizona; seasonal staffing; NHLR-registered 2001.

access.note: Summit trail listed open; the tower is an active lookout staffed in fire season; no source says visitors may climb the cab

visit.trail_note: 1.25 miles one way, from the trailhead at the end of Forest Road 340A; the register gives 1.5 miles

notes_for_editor: No build year is given beyond the Forest Service's early 1980s, so no built event is recorded. The 1913 plan is a newspaper report of a plan, not confirmation that a tower was built. The access level 'restricted' is our judgment from the trail being open and the lookout being an active staffed lookout; no source says whether the cab is open to visitors, so change it if the Tusayan Ranger District says otherwise. Record name, coordinates and elevation match the register. The Forest Lookouts page also carries a 1972 newspaper report of a violent death at the lookout shack; not used, because it concerns private individuals and says nothing about the lookout itself. The Wikipedia article repeats the register's design text and is not cited. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the earlier draft's sentence that an earlier structure may have stood on the butte but the sources describe none is removed, because a 1972 item on the Forest Lookouts page calls a 'Forest Service fire lookout shack on Red Butte', which predates the early-1980s tower. The story now says only that the sources do not say when a tower first went up. The 1972 item is not used in the story, and its crime report is not used at all; an editor may add the shack, without that detail, if wanted. The directions now name Forest Roads 320, 340 and 340A, as the Forest Service trail page gives them from Tusayan; the earlier draft named only 340A.
